# Git Gotchas

> Known git patterns that cause silent failures or hard-to-debug errors.

## Entries

- [git ls-files can't see untracked files](git-ls-files-blind-spot.md): Lint/check guards that enumerate via `git ls-files` skip new unstaged files and report a false green. MEDIUM.
- [Concurrent agents on one working tree: isolate your commit in a worktree](concurrent-shared-tree-worktree.md): A parallel session's stash/pull/rebase silently reverts your uncommitted edits and resets the index; recover via an out-of-repo backup patch + an isolated worktree cherry-pick of only your SHAs, and stage by explicit path (never `git add -A`). HIGH.
- [`git clone --branch <ref>` rejects a commit SHA (silent under set -e)](clone-branch-rejects-sha.md): `--branch` takes only a branch/tag name, so pinning to a bare SHA fails exit 128; with the clone redirected to /dev/null under `set -e` the script dies silently. Use `git init` + `fetch --depth 1 origin <ref>` + `checkout FETCH_HEAD`, which resolves branch/tag/SHA alike, and never hide fetch stderr. MEDIUM.
- [A hook committed as mode 100644 is silently skipped](hook-not-executable-silently-skipped.md): Git runs a hook only if it is executable, so a `.githooks/` hook tracked as 100644 never fires on any clone -- while `core.hooksPath` reads as set and running the script by hand works, making the guard look installed. Commit it as 100755 and verify by planting a real violation, since a guard that never runs is indistinguishable from one that passes. HIGH.
- [A version number read at task start is stale by commit time](stale-version-read-collides-on-push.md): In repos that hand-assign a version per commit, choosing it during the initial survey lets any push landing mid-session claim that number first. A rejected push is the LUCKY case -- if the concurrent commit touched different lines, the duplicate version merges cleanly and two commits ship claiming the same build. Re-derive the number after `fetch`/`rebase`, assert it is unclaimed, and re-sync all three sites (package.json, CHANGELOG heading, commit subject -- git never validates the subject). HIGH.
- [Verifying a GitHub write via raw.githubusercontent reports a lost update that never happened](raw-githubusercontent-stale-after-write.md): raw.githubusercontent is a CDN that can serve the pre-write blob for minutes and ignores cache-busting query strings, so a write-then-verify loop reports a missing commit that landed fine; the natural fix (re-PUT from the local copy) then destroys a concurrent peer's real commit. Verify with `gh api .../contents/...` and the path's commit log, not the raw URL. MEDIUM.
